proposals.content_angle: Explains Article 17 of Law 36/2024/QH15 (slow down and keep right on undivided roads; at narrow places the vehicle nearer a passing place yields; downhill yields to uphill; the vehicle with an obstacle ahead yields), parking on slopes under Article 18(2), the bans on overtaking near hilltops and U-turns on slopes, more safe distance on passes under Circular 38/2024, and the Decree 168/2024 Article 7(1)(h) fine.

proposals.working_title: Mit dem Roller auf die Fähre oder Pontonbrücke: Regeln in Vietnam
proposals.intent_rationale: Travellers on scooter trips in the Mekong Delta and the north cross rivers by ferry or pontoon bridge and want to know the queueing order, whether they must get off the bike on board and how boarding and leaving work.

proposals.working_title: Straßentunnel in Vietnam mit dem Roller: Licht an, nicht halten, nicht wenden
proposals.intent_rationale: Riders on longer trips pass through road tunnels and want to know the special rules inside: lights, no stopping, no U-turns and what to do if the scooter breaks down in a tunnel.
proposals.content_angle: Explains Article 26 of Law 36/2024/QH15 (low beam on in tunnels, no stopping or parking, emergency bays and warning signals after a breakdown, call the traffic police or tunnel operator), the bans on overtaking, U-turns and reversing in tunnels, and the Decree 168/2024 Article 7 fines for riding without low beam (600,000 to 800,000 VND), stopping in a tunnel and U-turns in a tunnel (800,000 to 1,000,000 VND).

distinct_from.reason: DE-S41 erklärt das Fahrverbot für Roller auf Schnellstraßen; dieses Thema behandelt die Regeln in Straßentunneln, die Rollern offenstehen: Licht, Halteverbot, Wendeverbot und Pannen.

proposals.working_title: Einsatzfahrzeuge in Vietnam: Was Blaulicht und Rotlicht bedeuten und wie Rollerfahrer Platz machen
proposals.intent_rationale: Visitors riding in Hanoi hear sirens and see flashing red or blue lights and want to know which vehicles have priority, what the colours mean and how to make way safely on a scooter.

proposals.working_title: Fußgängerüberwege in Vietnam: Wann Rollerfahrer halten müssen
proposals.intent_rationale: Riders in Hanoi constantly meet pedestrians crossing between scooters and want to know what the law requires at zebra crossings: when to slow down or stop, where not to stop or overtake and what failing to give way costs.
proposals.content_angle: Explains the pedestrian duties of riders in Law 36/2024/QH15 (slow down or stop when pedestrians or wheelchair users cross, also on green, Articles 11(4)(a) and 12(3)(a); no overtaking on crossings or while people cross, Article 14(6)(h) and (i); give way when turning, Article 15(3); no stopping on crossings, Article 18(4)(g)) and the Decree 168/2024 fines in Article 7(5)(b) (1,000,000 to 2,000,000 VND) and 7(2)(e).

proposals.working_title: Sicherheitsabstand mit dem Roller in Vietnam: Was das Gesetz verlangt
proposals.intent_rationale: Riders used to European traffic find vehicles in Vietnam riding very close together and want to know what safe distance the law actually requires and how to keep it in dense traffic and in rain.
proposals.content_angle: Explains the duty to keep a safe minimum distance in Article 12(1) of Law 36/2024/QH15, the distance table in Article 11 of Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT (for example 35 metres at 60 km/h on a dry road, more in rain, fog, on bends and passes), and the Decree 168/2024 fines for not keeping distance and causing a collision (600,000 to 800,000 VND under Article 7(3)(i), 10,000,000 to 14,000,000 VND when it causes an accident).

proposals.working_title: Spiegel, Licht, Hupe: Wofür Mieter in Vietnam ein Bußgeld riskieren
proposals.intent_rationale: Renters are often handed scooters with a missing mirror or a broken indicator and want to know whether they, as riders, can be fined for the bike's technical defects and what must work before they ride off.
proposals.content_angle: Explains Decree 168/2024 Article 14, which fines the rider, not the owner, for riding without a working horn, number-plate light, brake light, left mirror, indicators, headlight or brakes (400,000 to 600,000 VND) and without a registration certificate (2,000,000 to 3,000,000 VND), together with the documents a rider must carry under Article 56(1) of Law 36/2024/QH15, and turns this into practical checks at handover.

distinct_from.reason: Die Checkliste behandelt die praktische Fahrzeugübergabe beim Verleih; dieses Thema erklärt, für welche technischen Mängel der Fahrer selbst nach Artikel 14 der Verordnung 168/2024 belangt wird.

proposals.working_title: Notrufnummern in Vietnam: Polizei, Feuerwehr und Krankenwagen
proposals.intent_rationale: Travellers riding scooters in Vietnam want to save the right emergency numbers before setting off and know which number reaches the police, the fire service or an ambulance after an accident or breakdown.
proposals.content_angle: Explains Vietnam's emergency numbers (113 police, 114 fire and rescue, 115 ambulance, 111 child protection hotline) and what to say when calling, with the French foreign ministry's advice to call the police on 113 and contact the embassy after a serious accident, and practical tips for riders without Vietnamese.
